Supports the Director and Deputy Director of Industrial Base Pay (IBP) by performing complex data analytics of accounting, financial, and administrative data contained in IBP systems.
Serves as an analytical expert, demonstrating mastery of a wide range of qualitative and quantitative methods to assess and improve complex management processes. Measures program effectiveness and enhances organizational productivity.
Develops policies to integrate systematic data gathering and analysis into standard DFAS Operations, leveraging expert knowledge of financial processes, regulations, and systems to optimize the reliability and relevance of IBP data.
Represents the financial management community in meetings, committees with other organizations in connection with major policy and procedural matters, controversial issues, and matters involving financial management services.
Evaluates and makes recommendations concerning overall plans and proposals for complex financial and accounting projects impacting the accomplishment of DFAS strategic objectives. Establishes program evaluation criteria.
One year of specialized experience equivalent in level of difficulty and responsibility to that of the next lower grade (GS-13) within the federal service, which demonstrates the ability to perform the duties of the position, is required.

Specialized experience is defined as: Providing expert-level guidance to senior management related to planning, managing, executing, or assessing financial management program operations or projects, including conducting a variety of reviews, evaluations, and studies of financial management and accounting activities and systems to improve performance and efficiencies of overall program operations.

You may qualify for consideration if meeting specialized experience, education requirement, 90 days after competitive appointment requirement, and all other qualification requirements within 30 calendar days after the closing date of the announcement, unless otherwise indicated on the announcement.

Duties of the Supervisory Budget Analyst include but are not limited to: Reviews, edits, and consolidates annual and multi-year budget estimates for assigned organizations and program into an annual budget proposal.

Prepares or edits narrative justifications and projected funding needs and ensures that data in requests are formally and accurately documented in a wide variety of unrelated formats, schedules, and reports. Analyzes and forecasts operational budget for the facility and for changes in nature, type and cost of services produced.

Monitors the execution of a budget with many different sources and types of funding such as direct multi-year appropriations, allotments from many different appropriations, transfers of funds from other agencies, reimbursements for services performed. revenue from working capital funds, and trust accounts.

Reviews obligations, manages Fund Control Points (FCP), and prepares various reports timely. Serves are the direct supervisor of all VHSO Budget section employees. Plans work to be accomplished, sets priorities, and prepares work schedules. Assigns work based on the priorities and capabilities of subordinate staff.

Develops performance standards and conducts performance evaluations. Gives advice, counsel, and instruction to employees on both work and administrative matters.

Conducts special studies and analysis to develop required data and information for reporting purposes and prepares administrative reports/ responds to action items required by the AFO, CFO, VISN and VACO. Other duties as assigned.

Work Schedule: Monday - Friday, 08:00am - 4:30pm (Subject to change based on the needs of the Agency) Compressed/Flexible: Not Authorized Telework: Available Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

NOTE: Participation in the seasonal influenza program is a condition of employment and a requirement for all Department of Veterans Affairs Health Care Personnel (HCP). It is a requirement that all HCP to receive annual seasonal influenza vaccination or obtain an exemption for medical or religious reasons.

Wearing a face mask is required when an exemption to the influenza vaccination has been granted. HCP in violation of this directive may face disciplinary action up to and including removal from federal service.

HCP are individuals who, during the influenza season, work in VHA locations or who come into contact with VA patients or other HCP as part of their duties.

VHA locations include, but are not limited to, VA hospitals and associated clinics, community living centers (CLCs), community-based outpatient clinics (CBOCs), domiciliary units, Vet centers and VA-leased medical facilities.

HCP include all VA licensed and unlicensed, clinical and administrative, remote and onsite, paid and without compensation, full- and part-time employees, intermittent employees, fee basis employees, VA contractors, researchers, volunteers and health professions trainees (HPTs) who are expected to perform any or all of their work at these facilities.

HPTs may be paid or unpaid and include residents, interns, fellows and students. HCP also includes VHA personnel providing home-based care to Veterans and drivers and other personnel whose duties put them in contact with patients outside VA medical facilities.

As a Budget Analyst at the NH-0560-3 some of your typical work assignments may include: Serves as Senior Budget Analyst responsible for the overall administration and direction of the budgets and accounting processes.

Applies knowledge of the PPBE system, steering the development and defense of the Program Objective Memorandum (POM) to secure critical program funding.

As the program's financial authority, uses expert knowledge of the Financial Management Regulation (FMR), Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), and DFAR Supplement to support key decision recommendations.

Monitors, reviews, and analyzes the execution of approved budgets and program activities to optimize issuance of funding documents to meet mandated benchmarks and established program goals. Tracks all active funding for allocation, obligation, and expenditure of funds.

Extracts data from various systems to make financial recommendations and prepare and execute briefings.

1. Processes data and performs broad-in-depth financial analysis of interrelated accounting, military and civilian pay, accounts payable and receivable, and various travel entitlements to resolve especially difficult and sensitive, out-of-balance conditions associated with processing actions within Financial Management systems.

Analyzes and evaluates data to conduct a variety of fiscal reconciliations, reviews, and account adjustments. Analyzes diverse financial management technical methods, techniques, precedent cases, and procedures to resolve an extensive range of difficult financial issues or problems.

Resolves pay and entitlement problems unique to the customer. Manages and executes internal control procedures to protect against fraud, waste, and abuse.

(10%) Performs other duties as assigned.

The incumbent is responsible for overseeing all functions of Criminal Investigation's (CI's) budget. This entails coordinating and executing service-wide financial plans and labor costing.

In addition, the incumbent monitors, analyzes, and evaluates resource utilization for the financial plan and provides technical guidance and assistance relative to budgetary matters.

In concert with the Director Planning and Finance, the incumbent coordinates budgetary matters with the Department of Treasury, other Internal Revenue Service functions, the Division Information Officer, Information Systems, and other law enforcement agencies to keep abreast of practices, policies, and procedures which relate to CI's budget.

The incumbent directs budgetary programs, which require national coordination, and determines allocation of discretionary funds. The incumbent identifies operational deficiencies in criminal investigative programs, initiates corrective actions, and participates in program assistance and evaluation visitations of field offices.

In addition, he/she conducts reviews to identify effectiveness of program execution through analysis of management information, field narrative reports, and field visitations. STANDARD POSITION DESCRIPTIONS (SPD): PD26413 Visit the IRS SPD Library to access the position descriptions.

Build and maintain investment-grade models that can support executive decision-making, including detailed revenue builds, sensitivity analyses, valuation frameworks, synergy cases, downside scenarios, cohort economics, and ROI / payback analyses.

Proactively identify gaps in current reporting, model architecture, and decision-making processes, and build practical solutions that raise the quality of strategic finance support across the organization.

Strong commercial and strategic judgment, with the ability to evaluate not only what the model says, but what decision the business should make.

Skills
Technical Mastery: Highly proficient in Excel/G-Sheets; SQL experience is a plus.
AI & Automation: Proven track record of leveraging AI-driven tools and methodologies to streamline analytical workflows and optimize repetitive tasks.
SaaS Fluency: Deep understanding of SaaS economics and metrics (ARR, Churn, LTV/CAC).
Communication: Excellent verbal and written English; German is a bonus but not required.

The Interrogator: You don't just report numbers; you surface the story behind them and challenge assumptions at every level.
The Owner Mindset: You take full ownership of your workstreams and drive change in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.

## About Our Client ##
For a pioneering and fast-growing international group operating at the forefront of its industry, we are currently looking for a **Group Finance Manager**.
With around ten legal entities today, the group has experienced significant organic and external growth over the past few years. As the business continues to scale and increase in complexity, it is entering an exciting new phase of development.
To support this journey, we are creating a new leadership position within the Finance department. This role offers a unique opportunity to build, structure, and professionalize the finance organization while working closely with senior leadership in a highly entrepreneurial environment.
## Job Description ##
As Group Finance Manager, you will serve as the key link between the CFO and the accounting teams across the Group. You will play a critical role in strengthening financial operations, standardizing processes, enhancing reporting capabilities, and ensuring the scalability of the finance function as the organization continues to grow.
Initially, your focus will be on establishing robust financial processes, implementing a quarterly consolidation and management reporting framework, strengthening internal controls, and ensuring the delivery of high-quality financial information.
Over time, you will also contribute to the development of the Group's FP&A and controlling capabilities, helping transform Finance into a true business partner for operations and executive management.
This is a hands-on leadership role requiring strong technical expertise, operational pragmatism, and the ability to thrive in a dynamic and evolving environment.**Key Responsibilities**
**Financial Reporting, Consolidation & Closing Processes**
* Design, implement, and continuously improve Group-wide month-end and year-end closing processes.
* Establish and oversee a quarterly consolidation and management reporting process across all entities.
* Ensure the timely production of accurate and reliable financial information.
* Develop reporting packages and KPIs to support executive decision-making.
* Strengthen financial controls, reporting standards, and governance across the Group.
**Accounting Leadership**
* Lead and coordinate accounting teams located in Geneva and selected international subsidiaries.
* Supervise accounting operations to ensure compliance with local regulations and Group policies.
* Review and validate statutory financial statements and supporting documentation.
* Drive process harmonization and best practices across entities.
**Audit & Compliance**
* Coordinate and manage annual external audits across the Group.
* Act as the primary point of contact for external auditors and advisors.
* Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, statutory requirements, and internal policies.
* Support the implementation of scalable internal control frameworks.
**Tax & Treasury**
* Oversee tax compliance matters across the Group, including: VAT, Corporate income tax, Transfer pricing
* Coordinate with external tax advisors where appropriate.
* Identify and proactively manage tax risks and opportunities.
* Manage Group treasury activities in a multi-currency environment.
* Enhance cash forecasting and liquidity management processes.
* Support the CFO in financing initiatives and business expansion projects when required.
**Systems & Finance Transformation**
* Evaluate, implement, and enhance finance tools and systems to support the Group's growing needs.
* Lead finance transformation and process improvement initiatives.
* Promote automation, efficiency, data quality, and reporting capabilities.
* Ensure finance infrastructure remains scalable as the business expands.
**FP&A & Business Partnering (Medium-Term Focus)**
* Develop the foundations of a robust FP&A and controlling function.
* Support budgeting, forecasting, and long-term financial planning processes.
* Partner closely with operational leaders and the executive team.
* Provide insights and analysis to drive strategic and operational decisions.
* Help foster a performance-oriented and data-driven culture.
## The Successful Applicant ##

* University degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.
* Professional qualification (e.g., CPA, ACCA, Swiss CPA, Chartered Accountant, or equivalent) is highly desirable.
* 8+ years of progressive experience in finance and accounting roles within international and multi-entity environments.
* Proven experience managing financial reporting, consolidation, accounting operations, and audits.
* Previous experience in Switzerland is required.
* Strong understanding of tax matters, including VAT, corporate income tax, and transfer pricing.
* Experience in fast-growing, entrepreneurial, or private equity-backed environments is a strong advantage.

* Advanced financial systems and ERP knowledge.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
* Ability to design scalable processes and controls within a growing organization.
* Fluent French and English, both written and spoken, are required.
**Personal Attributes**
